target: Sejak kuliah di Bandung, adik saya tinggal di kamar kos dekat kampus.
english: Since studying in Bandung, my younger sibling has lived in a boarding room near campus.
grammar: Kos = a rented room in a shared house, classic student housing: kamar kos = boarding room.

target: Setelah menikah, mereka pindah dari kamar kos ke rumah kontrakan dua kamar.
english: After getting married, they moved from a boarding room to a two-bedroom rented house.
grammar: Kontrakan = a whole house you rent, usually yearly; kos = just a room: rumah kontrakan = rented house.

target: Harga kos di dekat kantor baru saya ternyata mahal sekali.
english: The price of a room near my new office turns out to be really expensive.

target: Ibu kos saya baik; kalau saya telat membayar beberapa hari, dia tidak marah.
english: My landlady is kind; if I am a few days late paying, she does not get angry.
grammar: Ibu kos = the landlady who runs a boarding house: bayar ke ibu kos = pay the landlady.

target: Biaya kos saya sudah termasuk listrik dan air, jadi pengeluaran gampang dihitung.
english: My room fee already includes electricity and water, so expenses are easy to calculate.

target: Kontrakan kami dibayar per tahun, jadi kami harus menyiapkan uang besar sekaligus.
english: Our rented house is paid for per year, so we have to prepare a large sum at once.

target: Sebelum menandatangani kontrak, cek dulu apakah harganya termasuk air dan listrik.
english: Before signing the contract, first check whether the price includes water and electricity.

target: Teman sekamar saya di kos sering lupa membayar iuran kebersihan.
english: My roommate at the boarding house often forgets to pay the cleaning dues.
grammar: Iuran = a regular fee everyone pays into: iuran kebersihan = the cleaning dues.

target: Anak kos biasanya memasak sendiri di akhir bulan supaya lebih hemat.
english: Boarding-house kids usually cook for themselves at the end of the month to be more thrifty.
grammar: Anak kos = someone living in a kos — shorthand for a tight budget: masakan anak kos = cheap cooking.

target: Pemilik kontrakan menaikkan harga sewa lima persen mulai tahun depan.
english: The owner of the rented house is raising the rent five percent starting next year.

target: Kami masih mencari kontrakan yang dekat sekolah anak-anak dan pasar.
english: We are still looking for a rental house near the children's school and the market.

target: Daripada mengontrak terus, lebih baik uangnya dipakai untuk mencicil rumah kecil.
english: Rather than renting forever, it is better to use the money to pay for a small house in installments.

target: Bulan depan kontrak kos saya habis, dan saya belum tahu mau memperpanjang atau pindah.
english: Next month my room lease runs out, and I do not know yet whether I want to extend or move.

target: Listrik di rumah kami pakai token, jadi harus diisi sebelum habis.
english: The electricity at our house uses tokens, so it has to be topped up before it runs out.
grammar: Token = prepaid electricity credit: beli token listrik = buy a code and punch it into the meter.

target: Tengah malam meteran berbunyi, ternyata token listriknya hampir habis.
english: In the middle of the night the meter beeped; it turned out the electricity credit was almost gone.

target: Saya selalu membeli token listrik seratus ribu setiap awal bulan.
english: I always buy a hundred thousand worth of electricity credit at the start of each month.

target: Kalau mati lampu, kami menyalakan lilin dan mengobrol di teras.
english: When the power goes out, we light candles and chat on the porch.
grammar: Mati lampu = a power cut of any kind, not just the lamps: sedang mati lampu = the power is out.

target: Angka di meteran listrik dicatat petugas setiap tanggal dua puluh.
english: The reading on the electricity meter is recorded by an officer on the twentieth of every month.

target: Mati lampu di daerah kami biasanya sebentar saja, paling lama satu jam.
english: Power cuts in our area are usually only brief, one hour at most.

target: Tagihan listrik kantor naik terus karena AC menyala sampai malam.
english: The office electricity bill keeps going up because the AC stays on until night.

target: Nomor meteran harus dimasukkan waktu membeli token lewat aplikasi.
english: The meter number has to be entered when buying electricity credit through the app.

target: Rumah kontrakan kami yang lama masih memakai meteran bulanan, bukan token.
english: Our old rented house still uses a monthly meter, not tokens.

target: Kulkas sempat mati waktu mati lampu kemarin, untung makanannya belum rusak.
english: The fridge went off for a while during yesterday's power cut; luckily the food had not spoiled.

target: Kata ayah, setrika dan pemanas air paling banyak memakan token listrik.
english: According to dad, the iron and the water heater eat up the most electricity credit.

target: Kami sengaja memilih AC baru yang katanya lebih irit listrik.
english: We deliberately chose a new AC that is said to use less electricity.

target: Waktu token habis tengah malam, minimarket dekat rumah jadi penyelamat.
english: When the electricity credit ran out in the middle of the night, the minimart near the house became the savior.

target: Air PAM di kompleks kami sering mati siang hari, jadi kami menampung air di ember.
english: The city water in our housing complex often goes off during the day, so we store water in buckets.
grammar: PAM = the city water utility: air PAM = tap water, used for washing rather than drinking.

target: Tagihan air PAM bulan ini lebih besar karena ada pipa bocor.
english: This month's city water bill is bigger because there was a leaking pipe.

target: Untuk minum kami pakai air galon; air PAM hanya untuk mandi dan mencuci.
english: For drinking we use gallon water; the tap water is only for bathing and washing.
grammar: Galon = the big 19-liter water bottle at home: air galon = drinking water from the dispenser.

target: Kalau air galon habis, tinggal telepon warung, nanti diantar sampai dapur.
english: When the gallon water runs out, just phone the corner shop, and it gets delivered right to the kitchen.

target: Satu galon isi ulang di depot dekat rumah harganya enam ribu.
english: One refill gallon at the depot near the house costs six thousand.
grammar: Isi ulang = refill: galon isi ulang = a refilled gallon from the water depot, cheaper than branded.

target: Abang galon langsung mengangkat galon kosong dan memasang yang baru.
english: The water delivery guy immediately lifted the empty gallon and installed the new one.

target: Pemakaian air kami bulan kemarin tinggi, mungkin karena banyak tamu menginap.
english: Our water usage last month was high, maybe because many guests stayed over.

target: Di kompleks kami, air PAM mengalir kencang hanya pagi dan malam hari.
english: In our complex, the city water flows strongly only in the morning and at night.

target: Ibu menyuruh kami menghemat air karena musim kemarau masih panjang.
english: Mom told us to save water because the dry season is still long.

target: Mereka membeli motor baru dengan DP tiga juta dan cicilan dua tahun.
english: They bought a new motorbike with a three-million down payment and two years of installments.
grammar: DP (say de-pe) = down payment: DP tiga juta = a three-million down payment. Also called uang muka.

target: Cicilan motor itu delapan ratus ribu per bulan, belum termasuk asuransi.
english: The installments for that motorbike are eight hundred thousand a month, not yet including insurance.
grammar: Cicilan = an installment; mencicil = pay bit by bit: cicilan dua tahun = two years of installments.

target: Kami menunda membeli kulkas baru karena masih ada dua cicilan berjalan.
english: We are putting off buying a new fridge because there are still two installment plans running.

target: Kalau uang mukanya lebih besar, cicilan bulanannya jadi lebih ringan.
english: If the down payment is bigger, the monthly installments become lighter.

target: Sisa cicilan rumah kami masih delapan tahun, pelan-pelan pasti lunas.
english: The remainder of our house installments is still eight years; slowly but surely it will be paid off.
grammar: Lunas = fully paid off: cicilannya sudah lunas = the installments are all paid.

target: Uang bonus akhir tahun langsung dia pakai untuk melunasi cicilan HP.
english: He immediately used his year-end bonus money to pay off his phone installments.

target: Jangan sampai menunggak cicilan, karena dendanya lumayan besar.
english: Do not let yourself fall behind on the installments, because the fine is quite big.
grammar: Menunggak = to fall behind on payments: menunggak cicilan = to miss installments.

target: Sebelum mengambil cicilan baru, hitung dulu semua pengeluaran bulananmu.
english: Before taking on a new installment plan, first count up all your monthly expenses.

target: Teman kantor saya menyesal mengambil cicilan mobil sebelum gajinya naik.
english: My office friend regrets taking on car installments before his salary went up.

target: Toko itu menawarkan cicilan tanpa bunga untuk pembelian di atas satu juta.
english: That store offers installments without interest for purchases above one million.
grammar: Bunga = flower AND interest: cicilan tanpa bunga = zero-interest installments.

target: DP rumah biasanya paling sedikit sepuluh persen dari harga rumahnya.
english: The down payment on a house is usually at least ten percent of the house price.

target: Arisan ibu-ibu di kompleks kami berkumpul setiap tanggal lima belas.
english: The neighborhood mothers' arisan in our complex gathers on the fifteenth of every month.
grammar: Arisan = a rotating savings club — all pay in, one takes the pot: ikut arisan = join one.

target: Nama ibu keluar waktu arisan dikocok, lumayan untuk membayar uang sekolah adik.
english: Mom's name came out when the arisan was drawn — helpful for paying my younger sibling's school fees.
grammar: Dikocok = shaken up and drawn by lot: nama ibu keluar = mom's name came out, she wins this round.

target: Banyak orang ikut arisan supaya bisa menabung sambil tetap bertemu teman-teman.
english: Many people join an arisan so they can save money while still meeting their friends.

target: Iuran arisan kantor kami dua ratus ribu, ditarik setiap tanggal gajian.
english: Our office arisan dues are two hundred thousand, collected every payday.

target: Ibu memakai uang arisan untuk membayar DP kulkas baru di toko elektronik.
english: Mom used her arisan money to pay the down payment on a new fridge at the electronics store.

target: Kalau dapat giliran pertama, uang arisan terasa seperti pinjaman tanpa bunga.
english: If you get the first turn, the arisan money feels like an interest-free loan.
grammar: Giliran = your turn in a rotation: dapat giliran pertama = get the first turn.

target: Setiap arisan selesai, ibu-ibu masih duduk lama membahas harga sembako.
english: Every time the arisan is over, the mothers still sit around a long time discussing staple food prices.
grammar: Sembako = the nine basic goods (rice, oil, sugar, and so on): harga sembako = staple prices.

target: Gaji pertama saya dulu di bawah UMR, tapi pengalamannya sangat berharga.
english: My first salary back then was below the regional minimum wage, but the experience was very valuable.
grammar: UMR = the regional minimum wage: di bawah UMR = below minimum wage.

target: UMR di Jakarta lebih tinggi daripada di kota kecil, tapi biaya hidupnya juga tinggi.
english: The minimum wage in Jakarta is higher than in small towns, but the cost of living is also high.

target: Setiap akhir tahun, pemerintah daerah mengumumkan UMR baru untuk tahun berikutnya.
english: Every end of year, the regional government announces the new minimum wage for the following year.

target: Gaji saya cukup untuk kebutuhan bulanan, sisanya saya tabung sedikit-sedikit.
english: My salary is enough for monthly needs; the rest I save bit by bit.

target: Gaji di kantor kami cair setiap tanggal dua puluh lima, langsung dipotong iuran.
english: The salary at our office comes through on the twenty-fifth, with dues deducted right away.
grammar: Cair, literally liquid = money comes through: gajinya sudah cair = the salary has landed.

target: Perusahaan kami menaikkan gaji sekali setahun, biasanya sesudah penilaian kerja.
english: Our company raises salaries once a year, usually after the performance review.

target: Selain gaji pokok, dia menerima uang makan dan uang transportasi.
english: Besides his base salary, he receives meal money and transport money.
grammar: Gaji pokok = base salary, before the extras: selain gaji pokok = on top of base salary.

target: Kata teman saya, gaji di pabrik baru itu sedikit di atas UMR.
english: According to my friend, the pay at that new factory is slightly above minimum wage.

target: Setelah tiga tahun bekerja di sana, akhirnya gajinya naik cukup besar.
english: After working there for three years, his salary finally went up quite a lot.

target: Gaji suaminya masuk ke rekening bersama untuk kebutuhan rumah tangga.
english: Her husband's salary goes into a joint account for household needs.

target: Kami membagi gaji ke tiga pos: kebutuhan, tabungan, dan hiburan.
english: We divide the salary into three categories: needs, savings, and fun.
grammar: Pos = a budget category: pos tabungan = the savings slot in the family budget.

target: Kakak saya hemat sekali; sepatu kerjanya dipakai sampai lima tahun.
english: My older sibling is really frugal; their work shoes get worn for up to five years.
grammar: Hemat = careful with money, boros = wasteful — everyday opposites: dia hemat sekali = very frugal.

target: Saya gampang boros kalau lapar; semua jajanan di pasar ingin saya beli.
english: I easily overspend when I am hungry; I want to buy every snack in the market.

target: Bulan ini kami harus lebih hemat karena ada biaya sekolah anak.
english: This month we have to be more frugal because there are the children's school costs.

target: Membawa bekal dari rumah jauh lebih hemat daripada membeli makan siang setiap hari.
english: Bringing a packed lunch from home is far more economical than buying lunch every day.

target: Dia kelihatan boros, padahal barang-barang mahalnya dibeli waktu diskon besar.
english: He looks like a big spender, even though his expensive things were bought during big sales.

target: Kata ibu, hemat itu bukan pelit, tapi tahu mana yang penting.
english: According to mom, being frugal is not being stingy, it is knowing what matters.
grammar: Pelit = stingy; hemat = sensibly careful: hemat itu bukan pelit = frugal is not stingy.

target: Langganan aplikasi yang jarang dipakai pelan-pelan membuat kita boros.
english: App subscriptions that are rarely used slowly make us wasteful.

target: Supaya hemat bensin, dia berangkat lebih pagi dan menghindari jam macet.
english: To save on fuel, he leaves earlier and avoids rush hour.

target: Kebiasaan kecil seperti mematikan lampu siang hari lama-lama terasa di tagihan.
english: Small habits like turning off the lights during the day eventually show in the bill.

target: Belanja bulanan kami biasanya di pasar dan supermarket dekat rumah.
english: Our monthly shopping is usually at the market and the supermarket near the house.
grammar: Belanja bulanan = the big monthly shop: uang belanja = the household shopping money.

target: Ibu selalu menulis daftar dulu supaya belanja bulanan tidak ada yang terlewat.
english: Mom always writes a list first so nothing in the monthly shop gets missed.

target: Beras, minyak goreng, dan sabun selalu ada di daftar belanja bulanan kami.
english: Rice, cooking oil, and soap are always on our monthly shopping list.

target: Belanja bulanan tanpa daftar ujung-ujungnya penuh barang yang tidak penting.
english: A monthly shop without a list ends up full of unimportant stuff.
grammar: Ujung-ujungnya = it always ends up: ujung-ujungnya boros = in the end you overspend.

target: Kami membandingkan harga di dua supermarket sebelum belanja bulanan yang besar.
english: We compare prices at two supermarkets before the big monthly shop.

target: Belanja sembako di pasar pagi lebih murah, tapi harus pintar menawar.
english: Shopping for staples at the morning market is cheaper, but you have to be good at bargaining.

target: Anak-anak senang ikut belanja bulanan karena boleh memilih satu camilan.
english: The kids love coming along on the monthly shop because they may pick one snack.

target: Sejak harga-harga naik, uang belanja bulanan kami sering kurang di minggu terakhir.
english: Since prices went up, our monthly shopping money often falls short in the last week.

target: Ayah kebagian tugas mengangkat semua kantong belanja dari mobil ke dapur.
english: Dad gets the job of carrying all the shopping bags from the car to the kitchen.

target: Harga cabai naik lagi, Bu? Rasanya kemarin masih setengah dari ini.
english: Chili prices are up again, ma'am? I feel like yesterday it was still half this much.
grammar: Chili prices are national small talk — they jump constantly: harga cabai naik lagi = up again.

target: Dulu lima puluh ribu cukup untuk seminggu, sekarang dua hari saja sudah habis.
english: Fifty thousand used to be enough for a week; now it is gone in just two days.

target: Menjelang hari raya, harga daging dan telur biasanya naik lebih dulu.
english: In the run-up to the big holiday, meat and egg prices usually go up first.

target: Ibu-ibu di warung sayur setiap pagi membahas harga minyak goreng.
english: The women at the vegetable stall discuss cooking-oil prices every morning.

target: Katanya harga gas tiga kilo mau naik lagi bulan depan.
english: They say the price of the three-kilo gas canister is going to go up again next month.

target: Harga kopi di kafe dekat kantor naik, jadi kami kembali ke kopi saset.
english: The coffee price at the cafe near the office went up, so we went back to sachet coffee.

target: Waktu semua harga naik begini, warung kecil bingung mau menaikkan harga atau tidak.
english: When all prices rise like this, small food stalls are not sure whether to raise prices or not.

target: Setiap harga BBM naik, ongkos angkot ikut naik pelan-pelan.
english: Every time fuel prices rise, minibus fares slowly rise along with them.
grammar: BBM = bahan bakar minyak, fuel: harga BBM naik = fuel prices went up — everything follows.

target: Untung gaji naik sedikit tahun ini, jadi kenaikan harga tidak terlalu terasa.
english: Luckily salaries went up a little this year, so the price increases are not felt too much.

target: Berapa ongkos angkot dari sini sampai terminal, Bang?
english: How much is the minibus fare from here to the terminal, sir?
grammar: Ongkos = fare, the cost of getting somewhere: ongkos angkot = the minibus fare.

target: Saya memilih toko yang lebih jauh karena ongkirnya gratis.
english: I chose the store that is farther away because its shipping is free.
grammar: Ongkir = ongkos kirim, the delivery fee; plain ongkos is a transport fare: gratis ongkir = free shipping.

target: Ongkir ke luar pulau bisa lebih mahal daripada harga barangnya sendiri.
english: Shipping to another island can be more expensive than the price of the item itself.

target: Kalau belanja di atas seratus ribu, aplikasi itu memberi gratis ongkir.
english: If you shop above one hundred thousand, that app gives free shipping.

target: Dulu ongkos bus ke kampung dua puluh ribu, sekarang hampir dua kali lipat.
english: The bus fare to the village used to be twenty thousand; now it is almost double.
grammar: Dua kali lipat = double: hampir dua kali lipat = almost twice as much.

target: Sopir travel menaikkan ongkos waktu musim liburan, katanya harga bensin juga naik.
english: The shuttle drivers raise fares during holiday season; they say fuel prices have gone up too.

target: Penjual online biasanya menulis bahwa harga belum termasuk ongkir.
english: Online sellers usually write that the price does not yet include shipping.

target: Saya menggabungkan dua pesanan dalam satu keranjang supaya ongkirnya lebih murah.
english: I combined two orders into one cart so the shipping would be cheaper.

target: Ongkos parkir langganan di gedung kantor dipotong langsung dari gaji bulanan.
english: The monthly parking fee at the office building is deducted straight from the monthly salary.

target: Kami patungan membeli kado pernikahan untuk teman satu tim di kantor.
english: We chipped in together to buy a wedding gift for a teammate at the office.
grammar: Patungan = to chip in together: kami patungan = we split the cost.

target: Untuk acara makan-makan akhir bulan, setiap orang patungan lima puluh ribu.
english: For the end-of-month get-together meal, each person chips in fifty thousand.

target: Anak-anak kompleks patungan membeli jaring baru untuk lapangan voli.
english: The kids in the complex chipped in to buy a new net for the volleyball court.

target: Daripada sewa mobil sendiri-sendiri, lebih murah kalau kita patungan satu mobil besar.
english: Rather than renting cars separately, it is cheaper if we all chip in for one big car.

target: Keluarga besar kami patungan membayar biaya rumah sakit kakek bulan lalu.
english: Our extended family chipped in to pay grandpa's hospital costs last month.

target: Kalau bensinnya patungan, perjalanan mudik naik mobil terasa lebih ringan.
english: If the fuel is split between everyone, the drive home for the holidays feels much lighter.

target: Uang patungan kemarin masih sisa tiga puluh ribu, mau dipakai untuk apa?
english: There is still thirty thousand left from yesterday's pooled money — what shall we use it for?

target: Target kami tahun ini menabung sepuluh juta untuk DP rumah kecil.
english: Our target this year is to save ten million for the down payment on a small house.

target: Sejak kecil, ayah mengajari saya menyisihkan uang jajan ke celengan.
english: Since I was little, dad taught me to set aside pocket money into a piggy bank.
grammar: Celengan = a piggy bank: menyisihkan uang ke celengan = set money aside in the piggy bank.

target: Dia menabung di rekening terpisah supaya uangnya tidak gampang terpakai.
english: She saves in a separate account so the money does not get spent by accident.

target: Kami menabung sedikit demi sedikit untuk biaya kuliah anak nanti.
english: We are saving little by little for the children's future college costs.
grammar: Sedikit demi sedikit = little by little: menabung sedikit demi sedikit = save bit by bit.

target: Uang receh di toples itu ternyata cukup untuk membeli kipas angin.
english: The loose change in that jar turned out to be enough to buy a fan.

target: Setiap gajian, dia langsung memindahkan uang tabungan ke rekening lain.
english: Every payday, he immediately moves his savings money to another account.

target: Tabungan liburan kami sempat terpakai waktu motor tiba-tiba masuk bengkel.
english: Our holiday savings did get used at one point when the motorbike suddenly went into the repair shop.

target: Menabung di awal bulan lebih mudah daripada menunggu sisa uang di akhir bulan.
english: Saving at the start of the month is easier than waiting for leftover money at the end of the month.

target: Nenek lebih percaya menyimpan uangnya di lemari daripada di bank.
english: Grandma trusts keeping her money in the wardrobe more than in the bank.

target: Saldo dompet digital saya tinggal lima ribu, nanti saya isi di minimarket.
english: My digital wallet balance is down to five thousand; I will top it up later at the minimart.
grammar: Isi saldo = top up a balance: saya isi di minimarket = I will top it up at the minimart.

target: Sekarang mengisi saldo bisa lewat aplikasi bank, tidak perlu antre di konter.
english: Nowadays topping up the balance can be done through the bank app; no need to queue at a counter.

target: Tukang parkir di pasar sekarang juga menerima pembayaran lewat dompet digital.
english: The parking attendants at the market now also accept payment through digital wallets.
grammar: Tukang = the ... guy, by trade: tukang parkir = parking attendant, tukang galon = the water guy.

target: Saya mengisi saldo dua ratus ribu setiap minggu khusus untuk ongkos ojek online.
english: I top up two hundred thousand every week just for online motorbike-taxi fares.

target: Membayar pakai dompet digital sering dapat potongan, tapi hati-hati jadi boros.
english: Paying with a digital wallet often gets you a discount, but be careful you do not turn wasteful.

target: Ibu akhirnya mau belajar memakai dompet digital supaya gampang membayar uang sekolah adik.
english: Mom is finally willing to learn to use a digital wallet so paying my younger sibling's school fees is easy.

target: Waktu sinyal hilang, dompet digital tidak bisa dibuka; untung masih ada uang tunai.
english: When the signal disappeared, the digital wallet could not be opened; luckily there was still cash.

target: Anak muda sekarang jarang membawa dompet karena semua pembayaran lewat HP.
english: Young people these days rarely carry a wallet because all payments go through their phones.

target: Mengisi saldo di minimarket biasanya kena biaya tambahan seribu rupiah.
english: Topping up a balance at the minimart usually incurs an extra fee of one thousand rupiah.
grammar: Kena biaya = get charged a fee: kena biaya seribu = charged one thousand.
